shortQuestions: Pakistan needs more technical education because its economy needs skilled workers — technicians, engineers and craftsmen — for industry, agriculture and services. General education produces many graduates who cannot find jobs, while technical education gives practical skills, self-employment and higher productivity.

After World War II both countries were ruined, but they invested heavily in technical and vocational training. Skilled workers rebuilt industries, produced high-quality goods (cars, machines, electronics) and exported them, so Japan and Germany quickly became industrial powers.

Linkage is necessary so that training centres teach the skills industries actually need, students get on-the-job training and apprenticeships, industries get trained workers, and the curriculum keeps up with new technology; it reduces unemployment and wastage.

Measures: more polytechnics and vocational institutes in every district; modern equipment and trained teachers; up-to-date curricula linked with industry; apprenticeship schemes; scholarships and loans; respect and good salaries for technical jobs; career counselling; and public-private partnership.

Technical education creates skilled manpower, raises industrial and agricultural production, encourages small businesses and self-employment, reduces unemployment and poverty, improves product quality for export, attracts foreign investment and lets Pakistani workers earn more abroad — all of which strengthen the economy.
activities: Sample argumentative essay — Need for Technical Education in Our Country: Opinion — Pakistan's progress depends on technical education. Supporting ideas: (1) Unemployment among general graduates is high, while industries lack skilled workers. (2) Developed nations such as Germany, Japan and China grew through technical skills. (3) Technical education promotes self-employment and small businesses. (4) Skilled workers earn foreign exchange. Counter-view — some think technical jobs have low status; but in reality they offer good income and respect. Conclusion — the government and society should make technical education attractive and accessible.

Group discussion points: why youth prefer white-collar jobs (social status, parents' wishes); disadvantages (unemployment, frustration); benefits of technical skills (jobs at home and abroad, own business); suggestions to change the trend (career counselling, awareness, better pay, success stories of skilled workers).
